rv.q: Just the dishevelled beauty of a self-contained omnishambles, a Schadenfreude nightmare brought to life by the sheer force of human incompetence.
It calls for acting larger-than-life and inch-perfect. It gets it.
Frayn's ingenious farce-within-a-farce sees a clunky touring production of a faded bedroom farce, Nothing On, fall apart around the performers' ears.
Michael Frayn’s uber-farce is technically dazzling but showing its age
Noises Off is classic farce, very well constructed, and as complex and silly as you would expect. It also, by default, feels quite dated.

cn.t: Critics praise this ingeniously constructed farce-within-a-farce for its excellent performances and masterful comic timing, with the cast delivering the larger-than-life, inch-perfect acting that Frayn's complex comedy demands.
